# Kiṁsīla Sutta (Snp 2.9 (PTS Snp 56))

**ID:** Snp 2.9 (PTS Snp 56)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Kiṁsīla Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kiṁsīla Sutta* (Snp 2.9) is the ninth discourse in the Cūḷavagga of the *Suttanipāta*, comprising verses 324–330 (PTS p. 56) [Müller 1881; Anderson and Smith 1913; Norman 1997-2001]. Metrically, the discourse is composed primarily in Triṣṭubh and mixed Triṣṭubh/Jagatī metres, alongside a mixed Triṣṭubh/Śloka verse (verse 327) and Śloka [Norman 1997-2001]. S.M. Katre identifies the sutta as an early Buddhist moral ballad aimed at inculcating ethical precepts [Katre 1931].

Opening with an inquiry concerning what kind of morality (*kimsīla*), conduct (*kimsamācāra*), and actions enable a person to become properly grounded and attain the ultimate goal (*uttamattha*) [Katre 1931; Anderson and Smith 1913], the sutta delineates the qualities and behaviors required to learn and reap the full benefit of the Dhamma. It emphasizes respect for elders, attentive and timely listening to well-spoken Dhamma discourses, and the mastery of tranquil understanding free from sloth, pride, and heedlessness [Müller 1881; Norman 1997-2001; Anderson and Smith 1913].
